214 UNREAD THIS MORNING. I ONLY HAD TO DEAL WITH 9.

8:00 AM. My Grok Bot goes through every unread email from the last 24 hours.

Three piles:

URGENT: needs me today. 9.
REPLY: needs me this week. 31.
FYI: no action. 174.

Every urgent one already has a reply waiting in Gmail Drafts. Written like me, because I showed it 20 emails I actually sent.

I edited 3. Sent all 9. 12 minutes.

Here's what nobody tells you: you don't have an email problem. You have a "which 9 matter" problem.

One prompt. 6 jobs:

→ SWEEP reads every unread thread from the last 24 hours
→ PILE sorts each one: URGENT, REPLY, FYI
→ WHY gives every thread one line: sender, subject, why it's in that pile
→ VOICE learned my writing from 20 emails I sent
→ DRAFT writes a reply for every urgent thread, in Gmail Drafts
→ GUARD never sends, archives, deletes or unsubscribes

Sweep reads. Pile sorts. I send.

The morning:
→ 08:00 routine runs
→ 08:01 214 unread
→ 08:03 9 URGENT · 31 REPLY · 174 FYI
→ 08:04 9 drafts in Gmail, in my voice
→ 08:04 one table: sender / subject / why
→ 08:20 I edit 3, send all 9
→ 13:00 second run: 46 new, 2 urgent

214 unread. 9 that mattered. 12 minutes.

Hard rules:
→ never sends, archives, deletes or unsubscribes
→ drafts only. Nothing leaves my outbox until I hit send
→ twice a day. Not every 10 minutes

Honest part: before the first run, paste in 15–20 emails you actually sent and say "learn my writing voice from these and save the rules." Skip that and the drafts sound like a robot. And every 10 minutes is how a week of usage disappears by lunch. (Demo numbers to tell the story. The setup is real.)

Paste this into Grok Bot ↓

"Go through my unread Gmail from the last 24 hours. Sort every thread into three piles: URGENT: needs me today. REPLY: needs me this week. FYI: no action. For every URGENT thread, write a reply in Gmail Drafts. Short, direct, in my voice. Show me the piles as a table: sender / subject / why, one line. Never send, archive, delete or unsubscribe."

Then: "Make it a routine for weekdays at 8 AM and 1 PM."

That's Job 2. The other 14 are in the guide below.

How many unread do you have right now? Be honest.

Bookmark this before you open your inbox ↓

note_tweet.text:
Everyone is suddenly selling us AI personal agents.

They'll book your flights, manage your emails, shop for you, handle your calendar and basically run your life.

Sounds great, right?

I spent weeks going through their tests, user experiences, reviews and privacy policies.

Here's what I found. And honestly, some of this shit is concerning. 

1 - Let's start with some actual failures:

• Meta's Muse got stuck on a "prove you're human" verification when trying to book a flight. A reporter wasted 30 minutes. He did it himself in 5.

• Another user tried using it for a visa application. Muse completed around 70%. They still spent an hour fixing uploads.

• In other words, the user still had to do the actual work.

2 - And it gets worse when you look at what you're giving up in return.

• Muse uses your chats to train its AI, ON by default.

• Its terms literally say you "bear all risk of financial loss" if it messes up with your money.

• It asks for full access to your accounts instead of limited access.

So you're trusting it with your accounts, your money and your personal information, while they make you bear the risk?

3 - More examples:

• Instinct pulled a login code from a user's Gmail WITHOUT asking, logged into their account and cancelled their event plans.

• It trains on your data by default.

• Its privacy policy says that even after deleting your account, it "may, but is not obligated to" delete your data.

Think about that for a second.

You're giving these companies access to your personal life, but apparently deleting your account doesn't necessarily mean deleting your data.

4 - Grok Bot:

• Gets full access to your apps. No read-only option.

• All your bots share one computer.

• Deleting a bot can leave its files and login sessions behind.

• In a shopping test, it successfully placed only 3 out of 8 orders.

We're being promised autonomous agents, but basic account isolation and shopping reliability are still problems.

5 - Poke:

• Kept automatically replying to emails even after the user repeatedly told it to stop.

• When asked to accept a simple calendar invitation, it couldn't do it and told the user to handle it themselves.

Imagine giving an AI permission to manage your inbox and having to fight it to stop sending emails.

6 - OpenClaw:

• Users report memory drifting, including forgetting information from just 20 minutes earlier in the same conversation.

• One security audit identified 512 security issues, 8 classified as critical.

• In one reported incident, it spammed a user's contacts with 500+ messages.

This is the kind of software people are being encouraged to connect to their entire digital lives.

7 - And the problems aren't limited to the big names.

• Asmi: Claimed a daily routine was active. It never ran once.

• HireAlpha: Kept spamming updates during tasks and couldn't book a hotel.

• Boski & Brea: Asked to book a hotel, they simply listed options and said they couldn't actually book.

• Shuffle: Links appeared blank in iMessage.

These aren't minor cosmetic issues. They're failures at the exact things these products advertise.

8 - And shopping? Let's look at the numbers.

One test put 25 AI agents through 200 real shopping orders.

Only 14% went through successfully.

The rest got stuck at checkout, crashed, ordered the wrong brand or got cancelled because the agent entered the wrong billing address.

9 - Here's what bothers me most about all of this.

Every company is marketing these agents as your personal assistant.

But look at what they actually need from you:

Your Gmail.
Your calendar.
Your files.
Your accounts.
Your payment information.
Your personal conversations.

They need you to connect everything before they can even begin proving they're useful.

And while the actual automation is still failing at basic tasks, they're already getting access to incredibly valuable user data.

10 - My biggest problem isn't that these agents make mistakes. They're new products, and mistakes are expected.

It's the gap between what they're marketing and what they're actually delivering.

They're selling autonomy, convenience and a personal assistant that knows you.

But right now, a lot of it looks like hype marketing designed to get users to connect their entire digital lives, generate more data and help these companies build their products.

We're being marketed the future of personal AI, but are we actually getting a personal assistant, or are we just becoming the product??

Introducing my first Grok @bot  suite - Wasp's Suite!

Wasp's Suite is based on my interests/needs and are designed to work independently or in conjunction with each other!

Wasp's Suite Bots:
-Space News Bot
-Starship Launch Prediction Bot
-3D Modeling Bot
-3D Print Prep Bot
-Wishlist Bot V2

Wasp's Suite is a series of bots that were built based on my personal interests and day to day work. 
All bots in Wasp's Suite are designed to work independently or in conjunction with each other for better outputs, be customized in any way you'd like, and optimize themselves to get better over time based on your needs. 
As more bots come out in Wasp's Suite, they will be able to be connected to existing bots as well! 

Also, all bots have the option to connect to Obsidian!

Space News Bot
Bot Link: https://t.co/QpbeJpYmEY

This news bot creates digests revolved around the space industry, primarily SpaceX by default. It can send multiple updates a day and includes all of the info any enthusiast needs! 

What it does - A space news desk that watches X accounts and news sources, and posts watch digests in chat.
Key features - Quick daily digest, SpaceX stories, Road Closures and FAA Notices, vehicle production progress, Starbase Louisiana updates, Construction Bids, Spaceflight news, optional launch prediction with Starship Launch Prediction Bot.

Starship Launch Prediction Bot
Bot Link: https://t.co/PRHbwysbCA

This bot does exactly what it sounds like, give an accurate window for when the next Starship launch will take place! This was tested for Flight 15 and was accurate within 3 days, many weeks before the official date was published.

What it does - Predicts upcoming launch dates based on historical data and current progress speed. 
Key features - Starship set by default with other rockets you can add, the next 3 flights each with confidence %, error and a date window, official sources first, and separate accuracy history per rocket. 

3D Modeling Bot
Bot Link: https://t.co/0QyOmGrsg9

This bot is meant for when you need quick 3D models made for 3D printing! Just draw a quick sketch of what you need, and this bot will turn it into a 3D model. It also is able to make changes to models, create renders to show off what you made, as well as work with the Print Prep Bot to get it optimized for 3D printing!

What it does - designs 3D models based on text, photos, and hand drawn sketches. Also assists in modifying existing models! 
Key features - Render and collage scripts, Gridfinity bins from a photo, fast design rounds, handoff to Print Prep Bot.

Print Prep Bot
Bot Link: https://t.co/OdOZ7b2Nov

This bot is made to help optimize slicer settings for 3D prints! It was made primarily for Bambu printers, but works with whatever slicer and printer you use! Just tell it what file you want to print and any other details you want to tell it, and it will optimize slicer/print settings for the print! If there's an issue with printing, take photos or tell it what went wrong and it will learn how your printer/filament behaves over time to get better results in the future!

What it does - Gets 3D print files ready to 3D print.
Key features - Edits 3MF and STL files, builds a calibration kit (cube and cylinder), keeps a lessons log, retries PC copies.

Wishlist Bot v2
Bot Link: https://t.co/MHBVEvZOZ2

This bot is meant to help you keep track of a wishlist! Just send it a link to any social media post, and it will find the item, link, price, and ratings, and save them to an easy to manage/read wishlist. It also is able to scan price tags so you don't have to look up what you want to buy in the future! All items can be categorized too!

What it does - Keeps a wishlist from product links you paste and photos of price tags.
Key features - Pulls in TikTok, Instagram, X, and other social media links, scans tags and labels, saves item/price/rating/links, categorizes items for easy category lookups.

I hope you all enjoy these bots! I've been training and using them for a while now, and built them with the intent of publishing. They're not perfect, but they work great for me and my needs on a day-to-day basis, and they're at a point where they're ready to be published.

I plan on building more bots in the future that connect to the suite, so if you want to see more or try any of them out, be sure to follow me here! 
I'm hoping of starting a trend of people publishing full suites of bots in the future as I think there is where @bot really shines!

If you have any feedback, please comment below so I can help make them better for y'all!

Also, check the comments for links to the Grok Bot Directory links!
